51443657.DESCRIPTION: Inhibition of TAM-3Y-F2Pmp peptide binding to N-terminal His6-fused STEP32 (282 to 563 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) by SPR analysis
51443657.original_paragraph: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed using a Biacore 3000 instrument (GE Healthcare) equipped with CMD500L sensor chips (XanTec Bioanalytics GmbH). Prior to immobilization of peptides, the sensor chip surface was conditioned by injecting a solution consisting of 10 mM sodium tetraborate, 1 M NaCl, pH 9.0, for 3 min at a flow rate of 20 μL/min. Then, the sensor surface was activated by injection of a 1:1 mixture of 50 mM NHS (N-hydroxysuccinimide) and 200 mM 1-ethyl-3-[3-dimethylaminopropyl]carbodiimide hydro- chloride (EDC) solutions from the Amine Coupling Kit (GE Healthcare) for 15 min at a flow rate of 5 μL/min. The peptides p3Y, p3Y-F2Pmp, 3Ysh-3-F2Pmp, and p-fin4 were dissolved in 10 mM sodium acetate pH 4.0 to 4−5 mg/mL. Next, each diluted peptide (4−5 mg/mL concentration) was injected on the activated surface of one flow cell at a 3−5 μL/min flow rate until the response was situated between 600 and 1100 RU. The first flow cell of each sensor chip was kept without peptide immobilization as a reference cell for background subtraction. For most cases, to get an optimal immobilization response, it was necessary to perform successive injections of the highly concentrated peptide. Deactivation of the unoccupied activated binding sites on the sensor was performed by injection of a solution of 1 M ethanolamine-HCl, pH 8.5, for 13 min at a 3 μL/min flow rate. All covalent immobilization steps have been performed at 25°C using degassed Milli-Q deionized water (Millipore) as a running buﬀer. After surface deactivation with ethanolamine, the immobilization level of each phosphopeptide was estimated from the sensorgrams and it varied between 105 and 1000 RU. Notably, we recorded only a very weak interaction with the analyzed phosphopeptides at concentrations of the injected peptides above 50 μM when STEP32 was immobilized on the sensor surface, even when we tested STEP32 immobilization on other sensors (Biacore Sensor Chip CM5 and NTA). For the interaction studies, the immobilized peptides were used as ligands, while the catalytic domain of the STEP enzyme, STEP32 (∼90% purity), was used as the analyte. The catalytically inactive mutant form, STEP32 C/S, was used for the interaction with p3Y and p-fin4 phosphopeptides, while the catalytically active form STEP32 WT was used for the interaction with F2Pmp-containing peptides. The initial concentration of the STEP32 protein was estimated using the Pierce 660nm Protein Assay Reagent (Thermo) and the FLUOstar Omega Microplate Reader (BMG LABTECH). For each kinetic experiment, a series of at least five diﬀerent concentrations of STEP32, ranging between 50 nM and 500 μM, were injected onto each peptide immobilized on the sensor chip, at a flow rate of 10 μL/min, in a random order. STEP32 concentrations were prepared as serial dilutions in HBS-EP buﬀer (0.01 M HEPES pH 7.4, 0.15 M NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 2 mM DTT, 0.005% v/v Surfactant P20). The association and dissociation time was set to 5 min. After each interaction test, 2−4 cycles of regeneration were performed by injecting 1 M NaCl in HBS-EP buﬀer for 2 min at a flow rate of 20 μL/min. All binding measurements were carried out at 25°C with HBS-EP as the running buﬀer. For p3Y, 3Y- F2Pmp, and 3Ysh-3-F2Pmp, the experiments were performed in duplicate and each STEP32 dilution was injected two times. In the case of the p-fin4 peptide, one binding experiment was performed and all STEP32 C/S dilutions were injected in duplicate. Nonspecific bindings were removed by separately subtracting the signal registered on the reference cell from the signal registered on each peptide- immobilized cell surface. The dissociation constant Kd values were calculated using GraphPad Prism 6.0 software by fitting the data to the regression-one-site specific binding model. All sensorgrams and steady-state plots shown in this manuscript as well as in the Supporting Information were prepared using Prism 6.0 (GraphPad Software).
